title: 3 · One run, end to end
description: One run, from all three stores at once. A run is `RUN_ID`, and it is spelled the same in each: `questions.run_id` on the rows, a Phoenix project named `<stage>-<run id>` on the spans, `run.id` on every log line. The rows say what the run produced and which gate stopped the rest; the spans say what the logic did and what it cost; the logs say literally everything else. Pick a run at the top.

list.name: run
list.label: Run
list.query: SELECT run_id AS "__text", run_id AS "__value" FROM questions WHERE run_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY run_id ORDER BY max(created_at) DESC

options.content:
**What this answers:** everything one `RUN_ID` did — what it produced, what it cost, its Phoenix projects and every line it wrote.

**The join between the three stores.** One run is `questions.run_id` on the rows, `<position>-<stage>-<run>` as a Phoenix project, and `run.id` on every log line.

panels.title: What the run produced
panels.description: Counted off the rows, which is where the truth about them is. Only live rows: a rerun deletes what it replaces, and a deleted run answers `make questions-diff` and not this.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "written",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'accepted') AS "accepted",
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'accepted') / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS "accepted %",
       count(DISTINCT topic_scope) AS "topics"
FROM questions
WHERE run_id = '$run'

panels.title: What the run cost
panels.description: The half SQL cannot answer. Every model call the run made, from its Phoenix projects. Spend is zero for a locally served model, which is the point of moving a judgement onto one.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "calls",
       sum(s.llm_token_count_prompt) AS "tokens in",
       sum(s.llm_token_count_completion) AS "tokens out",
       round(coalesce(sum(c.total_cost), 0)::numeric, 2) AS "spend",
       round((percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (
           ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM s.end_time - s.start_time)) * 1000)::numeric) AS "p95 call"
FROM projects p
JOIN traces t ON t.project_rowid = p.id
JOIN spans  s ON s.trace_rowid = t.id
LEFT JOIN span_costs c ON c.span_rowid = s.id
WHERE s.span_kind = 'LLM' AND p.name LIKE '%-$run'

panels.title: Where the questions went
panels.description: Every gate that refused something, and `accepted`. The last gate that ran is the one that refused it, because the checker returns on the first failure.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(rejected_reason, status) AS gate, count(*) AS questions
FROM questions
WHERE run_id = '$run'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: What the calls were for
panels.description: The Pydantic shape each call asked for, which is what `tag.tags` carries. This is the query `make spend-by-shape` reads log prose to answer. Empty for a run made before the shape was put on the span.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT btrim(replace(coalesce(
           s.attributes->'tag'->>'tags', '["untagged"]'), '_', ' '), '[]" ') AS shape,
       s.attributes->'llm'->>'model_name' AS model,
       count(*) AS calls,
       round(coalesce(sum(c.total_cost), 0)::numeric, 4) AS spend,
       round(avg(extract(epoch FROM s.end_time - s.start_time) * 1000)::numeric) AS mean
FROM projects p
JOIN traces t ON t.project_rowid = p.id
JOIN spans  s ON s.trace_rowid = t.id
LEFT JOIN span_costs c ON c.span_rowid = s.id
WHERE s.span_kind = 'LLM' AND p.name LIKE '%-$run'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY calls DESC

panels.title: Its Phoenix projects
panels.description: One per stage that ran under this id, with the span count and the window it covers. A run of the whole pipeline is several rows; one restarting worker used to be thousands.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT p.name AS project,
       count(s.id) AS spans,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.status_code = 'ERROR') AS errors,
       min(s.start_time) AS started,
       max(s.end_time) AS ended
FROM projects p
JOIN traces t ON t.project_rowid = p.id
JOIN spans  s ON s.trace_rowid = t.id
WHERE p.name LIKE '%-$run'
GROUP BY p.name
ORDER BY spans DESC

panels.title: Gate verdicts recorded in Phoenix
panels.description: The annotations behind Phoenix's Evaluations view, which is the half that is easy to lose: they are best-effort, and one refusal disables them for the rest of the run. Empty here against a non-empty panel on the left means the run produced questions and recorded no verdicts.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT a.name AS annotation,
       a.annotator_kind AS kind,
       count(*) AS scored,
       round(avg(a.score)::numeric, 3) AS "mean score"
FROM span_annotations a
JOIN spans   s ON a.span_rowid = s.id
JOIN traces  t ON s.trace_rowid = t.id
JOIN projects p ON t.project_rowid = p.id
WHERE p.name LIKE '%-$run'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Every line this run wrote
panels.description: The run's own lines, across every process it crossed, at every level. This is the other half of the separation: Phoenix holds what the logic did, and this holds everything — the HTTP, the SQL, the object store, the retries. A line's `trace.id` opens its span in Phoenix.
